chunks: What "FR4" means. The question: What does "FR4" mean?
FR-4 is the standard material most circuit boards are made from.
It is woven glass cloth soaked in epoxy resin and baked hard, with a flame retardant added so it stops burning when a flame is removed. The name does not mean four layers.
The 4 is just an old grade number.
Think of a fiberglass boat hull. Glass cloth gives the strength and stiffness, and hardened resin glues the cloth into one solid sheet and keeps it from soaking up water.
FR-4 is the same kind of sheet, thin and flat, with copper bonded to its faces. The flame retardant is an extra ingredient in the resin.
The analogy breaks in one place: flame retardant means "stops burning on its own", not "fireproof".
Left, the structure: woven glass yarns (the two yarn directions, drawn in two colors) with epoxy filling the spaces.
Right, the name: FR for flame retardant, 4 for the grade number.
The sibling G-10 is the same composite without the flame retardant, so it is flammable and rarely used for modern PCBs.
Flame retardant (FR): formulated so the material self-extinguishes. UL 94 volts-0 is the usual rating. Epoxy: the resin that hardens to bond the glass and insulate.
Glass cloth: woven glass fiber that gives strength and stiffness ("PCB layers and their materials"). G-10: the same glass and epoxy sheet with no flame retardant.
Glass transition temperature ( T g ): the temperature where the resin turns soft. Standard FR-4 is about 130 to 140 degrees Celsius ("PCB insulation materials and trade-offs").
Take a bare FR-4 sheet 100 mm by 100 mm and 1. 6 mm thick. Its volume is 10 cm times 10 cm times 0. 16 cm = 16 cm³. At about 1. 85 g/cm³ it weighs about 30 g. A standard 0.
035 mm copper foil on both faces would add only about 6 g. It is cheap, stiff and easy to drill and plate, which is why almost every ordinary board uses it.
That is the whole idea.
"FR-4 means Flame Retardant grade 4. FR means the laminate is self-extinguishing, tested to UL 94 volts-0; the 4 is just a grade number in the NEMA system, not four layers.
It's woven fibreglass in epoxy resin, the standard PCB substrate: strong, cheap, easy to process, with a dielectric constant around 4. 3, loss tangent around 0.
02, and a glass transition around 130 to 180 degrees depending on grade. It's the flame-retardant version of G-10."
